title: Weekly POC stability & rollback drill with Zenara Pharma
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-09 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Aisha Monroe, Ravi Anand (Redwood); Marta Ruiz, Ethan Cole, Lena Park, Samir Patel (Zenara)
Links shared: deck: https://redwood.app/decks/zenara-poc; benchmark spreadsheet: https://sheets.example/zenara-bench

Summary:
A short drill to validate stability signals from last week's run, and execute a planned rollback simulation (canary -> fallback to hosted). Discussed a small regression in prompt set A2, tightened guardrail thresholds, and agreed next steps to run dedicated throughput benchmarks. Decided to surface SOC2/SAML artifacts to legal and schedule a 1-hr deep performance test next Tue.

Topics:
- Stability signals & error spike at 03:12 in last run
- Rollback/fallback playbook validation
- Prompt set regression (A2) and scoring drift
- Guardrail thresholds & false-positive tuning
- Dedicated vs hosted latency tradeoffs

Transcript:
[00:00] Aisha Monroe: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call, and we'll jump to the stability slides, Ravi has the logs.
[00:18] Marta Ruiz: Hey, Marta here. We're short on Sam today but Sam joined for the SRE bits.
[00:25] Ethan Cole: Ethan here.
[00:27] Lena Park: Lena.
[00:30] Ravi Anand: Hi, Ravi from Redwood, I'm going to share the error heatmap and KV cash -- I mean KV cache traces.
[00:38] Samir Patel: Samir, SRE, all good.
[00:42] Aisha Monroe: Cool. So objective: run the rollback simulation, confirm we hit our SLOs, and triage the small prompt drift you called out last week.
[00:52] Ravi Anand: Slide 3 shows the last 24-hour window; most tokens look fine, there's a spike around 03:12 UTC where the per-token lat increases and we got 4x 502s in a two-minute span. The stack shows a transient GPU OOM on a dedicated node during a long-context job.
[01:12] Marta Ruiz: Right, that was from a batch job that we didn't flag as long-context. Question: was that on Redwood Dedicated or hosted?
[01:20] Ravi Anand: That was dedicated pool A, yes. On hosted we didn't see the same OOMs because the request was split differently.
[01:29] Ethan Cole: Can you remind us of the exact config for dedicated pool A? Memory/quantization?
[01:36] Ravi Anand: We're running a 24GB A100 equivalent, model is a quantized v1.3 with 8-bit GEMM. There's a slightly aggressive KV prefetch that caused memory pressure with concurrent long-context.
[01:48] Lena Park: So is the fix to reduce batch size or change prefetch? What's the customer-facing change?
[01:53] Ravi Anand: Short term we throttle long-context batches and apply an auto-rollback to a hosted-compatible model variant if memory exceeds threshold. Long-term we adjust kernel selection to reduce prefetched KV.
[02:04] Marta Ruiz: Ok. Let's run the rollback drill now, step-by-step so Samir can validate.
[02:10] Samir Patel: Ready.
[02:12] Aisha Monroe: Step 1: trigger canary overload scenario (Ravi please).
[02:17] Ravi Anand: Kicking off synthetic workload now. I'm pushing a mix of short and long prompts, with 20% long-context.
[02:28] [04:35] Ravi Anand: (status) Canary latency climbs to 220ms p50, p95 2.4s, and we see a few queue rejects. At threshold we trigger routing policy: fallback to hosted variant in us-east-1.
[04:50] Lena Park: Do we preserve tokens/kv state on fallback? Is there a continuity impact?
[04:56] Ravi Anand: There's a small cold-start on the hosted variant, kv cache isn't transferred across model variants; we rely on prefix cache so you might see a single-turn quality blip but no data loss.
[05:12] Marta Ruiz: That's acceptable as long as we can show the fallback path and SLOs.
[05:18] Aisha Monroe: Noted. Samir, did the rollback route come up in your infra logs?
[05:23] Samir Patel: Yep, I see the policy trigger and the fallback. I also saw an alert to PagerDuty that we need to silence for tests. We should tag test runs.
[05:33] Ethan Cole: On the call last week we saw a scoring drift for prompt set A2 — any light on why?
[05:39] Ravi Anand: We compared evals from the checkpoint on 09/01 vs latest. There's a small metric delta: A2 precision dropped from 0.87 to 0.81 on the specialist scoring rubric. Looking at examples, the model's stop-token handling changed and the reranker bumped a different candidate. Could be quantization edge-case.
[06:03] Lena Park: Can you show an example?
[06:06] Ravi Anand: Sure, example 4 in the sheet: expected label "dosage-adjustment" and model emitted a longer free-text that caused the scorer to downweight it.
[06:16] Marta Ruiz: Is this regress-only on dedicated? Or also seen on hosted?
[06:20] Ravi Anand: We repro on both, but it's more frequent when KV cache is cold — so fallback cold-starts increase incidence.
[06:30] Aisha Monroe: So mitigations: add a prompt template guard to enforce output format, and adjust scorer tolerance threshold from 0.75 to 0.70 for A2. Any objections?
[06:42] Ethan Cole: I worry about false-positive acceptance — lowering thresholds might accept bad outputs elsewhere.
[06:47] Ravi Anand: We can scope that threshold change only to A2 and add a higher-weight strictness for other critical intents. And add a post-process sanitizer that enforces label tokens.
[06:59] Lena Park: Sounds reasonable.
[07:02] Marta Ruiz: Also we want an audit trail for changes — can you log prompt template versions and scorer configs?
[07:08] Aisha Monroe: Yes, Redwood console keeps that; we'll share the config export.
[07:12] Ravi Anand: I'll attach the rollback playbook and the config diffs to the spreadsheet after this call.
[07:18] Samir Patel: One more infra note: during the simulated rollback I saw a slight region mesh latency when the load shifted to hosted in us-east-1; if traffic is cross-region we might want to prefer same-region fallback.
[07:30] Ravi Anand: Good point — routing policy can be region-preferential; we'll change to prefer same-region hosted pools first.
[07:36] Ethan Cole: Can we quantify expected token-cost delta for fallback? We need to show cost impact to finance.
[07:42] Ravi Anand: Roughly +12% per-token cost during fallback since hosted variant is smaller throughput optimized but not as cheap as dedicated steady batching. I'll add more precise numbers in the benchmark sheet.
[07:52] Aisha Monroe: Ok, let's move to guardrail tuning: Marta flagged a false-positive where the safety filter blocked legitimate chemical formulation questions.
[07:59] Marta Ruiz: Yes, the filter flagged an internal doc phrase; it's a false positive. We need narrower safety signatures for internal domain language.
[08:07] Ravi Anand: We recommend adding allowlist rules for Zenara's drug-term tokens and a higher-score threshold for external publication blockers.
[08:16] Lena Park: How does Redwood's safety rule set handle domain allowlists?
[08:20] Ravi Anand: There is a per-account allowlist in console; we can push a curated token list. Also we can push a guardrail snapshot to your security Slack channel for review.
[08:31] Marta Ruiz: Perfect.
[08:34] [12:05] Aisha Monroe: Quick check — legal asked for SOC 2 artifacts and SSO/SAML metadata. Who owns sending those?
[12:12] Ravi Anand: I'll post the SOC 2 cert and SAML metadata to the secure folder, but legal should request via the secure artifact workflow.
[12:20] Marta Ruiz: We'll ask legal to request, yes.
[12:24] Ethan Cole: Also, for the long-term architecture, we need a private deployment option — can Redwood run in our VPC?
[12:31] Aisha Monroe: Yes, Redwood Private supports VPC and on-prem packages; there's an enterprise onboarding timeline of 6-8 weeks typically.
[12:38] Samir Patel: For VPC we'll need HSM/KMS integration.
[12:41] Ravi Anand: Supported — we have KMS/HSM connectors and audit log export; we'll share the connector docs.
[12:50] Lena Park: Great.
[12:52] [18:10] Marta Ruiz: Back to the regression: what's the immediate triage plan?
[18:15] Ravi Anand: Step A: narrow prompt set A2 and run A/B evals with old score threshold. Step B: test the prompt-template sanitizer. Step C: run dedicated throughput benchmark next week and measure failure modes.
[18:27] Aisha Monroe: Let's lock owners.
[18:30] Ravi Anand: I'll run the A/B evals and post the result by Monday EOD.
[18:35] Marta Ruiz: I'll validate the examples and confirm which intents are critical.
[18:38] Samir Patel: I'll run the rollback network test (region-preferential) and share logs.
[18:44] Ethan Cole: Finance wants the cost delta numbers; we'll need a small table.
[18:48] Aisha Monroe: Ravi can produce that from the benchmark.
[18:51] Lena Park: Can we schedule the 1-hour performance deep test next Tuesday?
[18:55] Aisha Monroe: Yes, propose 2026-09-15 14:00 UTC in the sheet.
[18:59] Marta Ruiz: Works for me.
[19:02] [27:10] Ravi Anand: NOTE: I just pushed a small hotfix to scorer config to avoid stop-token drift; it's a config toggle, not a model re-train. We'll watch for regressions.
[27:20] Marta Ruiz: Thanks.
[27:25] Aisha Monroe: Any outstanding blockers from anyone?
[27:29] Samir Patel: Just the PagerDuty noise during tests — we need a test-suppress policy.
[27:34] Ravi Anand: We'll create a test tag for alerts.
[27:38] Ethan Cole: Legal will formalize the SOC2 artifact request.
[27:42] Lena Park: Product wants to see guardrail false-positive examples after threshold change.
[27:46] Aisha Monroe: We'll deliver.
[27:49] [34:03] Marta Ruiz: One process ask — can Redwood provide a short runbook snippet describing rollback visible to our on-call?
[34:10] Ravi Anand: Yes, 1-pager runbook will be posted to the shared folder.
[34:14] Aisha Monroe: Ok, last thing: recap and owners.
[34:18] Aisha Monroe: Recap: Ravi to run A/B evals and bench; Samir to run rollback region test; Ravi to push guardrail allowlist; Aisha to share SOC2/SAML path; schedule deep perf test 09/15.
[34:35] Marta Ruiz: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[34:38] Ethan Cole: Thanks.
[34:40] Lena Park: Bye.

End of transcript.
summary: Rollback drill successful: routing policy triggered and fallback worked but cold-start caused minor quality blips. Small regression in prompt set A2 reproduced; mitigations agreed (prompt sanitizer, scoped scorer threshold). Action owners assigned for benchmarks, rollback region test, and SOC2/SAML artifact transfer. Deep perf test scheduled for 2026-09-15.
action_items: Ravi Anand - run A/B evals and post results - 2026-09-13
Ravi Anand - produce per-token cost delta table for fallback - 2026-09-13
Samir Patel - run region-preferential rollback network test and share logs - 2026-09-11
Aisha Monroe - share SOC2 and SAML metadata link to Zenara legal - 2026-09-10
Ravi Anand - push guardrail allowlist and guardrail snapshot to security Slack - 2026-09-11
Redwood - post 1-pager rollback runbook in shared folder - 2026-09-10
next_steps: Run dedicated throughput benchmark and compare with hosted baseline
Legal to request SOC2 via secure artifact workflow
Product to review guardrail false-positive examples after threshold change
